source_title: Every Scream Movie, Ranked By Kill Count
source_excerpt:
What good is a slasher movie without a high kill count? While the Scream films have a lot going for them, including their sharp sense of humor, innovative self-aware tone, and compelling whodunnit elements, horror fans expect a lot of burials for their buck, and so the long-running franchise has never skimped on the slayings. Even so, each new Ghostface murder spree is different from the last, so the total kill count varies from one movie to the next.
It's common for horror franchises to get bigger and bloodier with each new installment, but the S cream series is nothing if not subversive, so its kill counts don't necessarily increase every time. Some of the earlier films in the franchise are still among the goriest, while some of the latter entries might be less lethal than fans would expect. There are numerous ways to rank the Scream movies, from critical reception to box office gross, but this is the metric that matters most to slasher addicts. Here is every Scream film ranked by kill count.
The Scream franchise got off to a beautifully bloody start with the seminal 1996 original, which sports a none-too-shabby kill count of eight. Part of the macabre magic of the first Scream movie is that it wastes no time in wracking up the dead bodies, with both Casey Becker (Drew Barrymore) and her boyfriend, Steve, killed off in the film's iconic opening scene.
The gore-soaked climax at the Macher house then sees Ghostface claim two more victims — Tatum Riley and cameraman Kenny — before Sidney Prescott and Gale Weathers take out killers Billy and Stu. The other on-screen death comes from the stabbing of Principal Himbry (Henry Winkler), in a scene that was deliberately added into the movie to insert another kill halfway through.
The film's eighth death actually happens off-screen prior to the film's events — the murder of Sidney's mother, Maureen, by Billy Loomis. Maureen's demise casts a huge shadow over the story, so fans usually include it in the movie's kill count. But if only the on-screen kills are recognized, then the first Scream 's total goes down to seven.
2022's Scream mirrors the original in so many clever ways — e.g. the third act returning to the Macher house and one of the killer's turning out to be the protagonist's boyfriend. Whether by accident or design, another way the two films are alike is that they have the exact same kill count. Although Scream '22 features an indisputable eight on-screen kills.
It actually takes the legacy sequel a little while to get its kill count going, seeing as — uniquely for this franchise — nobody actually dies in its opening sequences. Jenna Ortega's Tara Carpenter is badly injured, but she miraculously survives to become the co-lead of the next two movies.
The first on-screen death belongs to Vince Schneider (Kyle Gallner), who is brutally targeted by Ghostface in a parking lot. The rest of the kills occur across three big set pieces — Sheriff Judy and her son, Wes, at the Hicks residence, Deputy Clay and Dewey Riley (R.I.P.) at the hospital, and Liv and the killers, Richie Kirsch and Amber Freeman, in the third act.
Scream 2 lived up to its name by featuring two extra kills than its predecessor. In actuality, the same number of major characters die as in the first one, but a couple of additional minor characters are killed off in order to facilitate the sequel's most nail-biting sequence.
The opening sequence executes Jada Pinkett Smith's Maureen and her boyfriend Phil, before Cici Cooper (Sarah Michelle Gellar), fan-favorite Randy Meeks , Hallie, and Derek join them throughout the rest of the movie. The killers, Nancy Loomis and Mickey Altieri, are then defeated by Sidney, Gale, and Cotton Weary at the climax.
The two minor characters who bump up the total are Officer Andrews and Officer Richards, who are assigned to escort Sidney and Hallie to safety but end up murdered by Ghostface. The resulting scene, in which the two women have to crawl over the killer's prone form to escape through the front window of the cop car, is one of the Scream series' tensest moments.
Although horror tropes indicate that each Scream movie should feature more kills than the last, Scream 3 surprisingly bucks that trend by having the exact same kill count as the second film. That said, this time all 10 on-screen deaths are important, named characters. Likewise, as there is only one Ghostface this time around, nine of those are the killer's victims. That makes Roman Bridger the deadliest Ghostface of the original trilogy.
The first script written for Scream 3, which was rejected by execs, featured the return of Matthew Lillard as Stu Macher, a concept that later materialized in Scream 7 .
Recurring character Cotton and his girlfriend Christine are murdered in the opening sequence, with the cast of Stab 3 picked off across the rest of the film. Namely, Sarah Darling, Tom Prinze, Angelina Tyler, Tyson Fox, and breakout character Jennifer Jolie (Parker Posey). Other victims include Patrick Warburton's bodyguard Steven Stone and corrupt movie producer John Milton. Sidney then finishes off her evil half-brother Roman in the final act.
After two movies starring the Carpenter sisters, Scream 7 was very much the franchise going back to its factory settings by re-centering the story on Sidney once again. At the same time, the franchise also returned to the same kill count sported by both Scream 2 and Scream 3 . The film depicts 10 deaths in total, although one of them happens off-screen and three of the victims are Ghostfaces.
Horror fans Scott and Madison are murdered in the Macher house in the opening, before Tatum Evans' friends Hannah, Chloe, Ben, and Lucas are mown down throughout the rest of the runtime. Aaron also has his throat slit off-screen shortly before McKenna Grace's Hannah is killed on stage.
The film's most subversive death is the demise of Karl Gibbs halfway through, thereby unmasking one of the film's three Ghostfaces. It isn't until the finale that Sidney and her daughter discover Anna Bowden and Marco Davis are the other two killers. As for what happens to that pair, let's just say you should never mess with the Prescott women.
Depending on the criteria, Scream 4 is either the most bloodthirsty Scream movie of the series, or the second most. The confusion stems from the fourth film's uniquely meta intro, which plays out the opening sequences of fictional movies Stab 6 and Stab 7 before the real events of Scream 4 actually start. Three fictional characters die in these scenes — Trudy, Sherrie, and Rachel (Anna Paquin), as killed by Chloe (Kristen Bell).
Whether these fictional deaths should contribute to the kill count, then, is up for debate. Even without counting those fakeout deaths, Scream 4 squeezes a lot of murder into its runtime. This is in part thanks to the large intergenerational cast of characters. The teen characters to die include Marnie, Jenny, Olivia, Robbie, and Trevor, while the offed adult characters include Alison Brie's Rebecca, Kate Roberts, and Deputies Hoss and Perkins (Adam Brody). At one point, Kirby Reed would have been included, as well, but Scream VI later revealed that she survived her stabbing.
Those under the Ghostface mask for this killing spree are Charlie Walker and Jill Roberts, Sidney's cousin. Jill is the first Ghostface to kill another Ghostface, as she betrays and murders Charlie, before Sidney ultimately kills her.
When it comes to on-screen, non-fictional deaths, Scream VI clears the rest of the franchise to claim the crown for the Scream movie with the highest kill count. This is appropriate as the 2023 release was hyped up as being the most brutal entry in the slasher series yet, with Ghostface portrayed wielding a wider array of weapons than usual — including, for the first time, firearms.
Scream VI 's kill count is boosted by the super-sized approach the movie takes to each franchise trope. Three victims instead of two die in the opening scene — Samara Weaving's Laura Crane and two wannabe Ghostfaces (Jason and Greg) that are killed by the real one. Similarly, instead of one or two Ghostfaces unveiled and unalived in the finale, there are three — Detective Bailey, Quinn, and Ethan, revealed to be Richie's family out for revenge.
As for the movie's middle, an eclectic range of characters are killed as the Ghostfaces pursue the Carpenters. These include Sam's therapist Dr. Stone, Gale's boyfriend Paul, Mindy's girlfriend Anika and Quinn's lover Brooks. In addition, two unfortunate customers and a clerk are left deceased after Ghostface shoots up a bodega. With Scream 8 in the works, it remains to be seen for how long Scream VI can defend its title as the most lethal Scream of them all.
